This update marks the start of the Fairy Dust Festival test! We've been working on getting the festivals ready, and Early Access players are now invited to partake in the first of these seasonal festivals and share their feedback!

One of Wenngrove's seasonal traditions, the Fairy Dust Festival celebrates the Spring Equinox and the coming of spring blooms with splashes of vibrant colour and decorations! Speak with the governor, Sulo, to hear all about the town's tradition. During the festival period, townsfolk will have new quests for you, and you'll be able to harvest new items including Daffodils, Fiddleheads, and Maple Syrup - it's a great time to plant a Maple Tree and collect the syrup with a Tree Tap! Your livestock may also produce more items thanks to the Twitterpated buff.

The locals have hidden painted Fairy Eggs around town for people to find. Collect them to exchange for prizes at the festival stall in the town square! Many items are only available during this time each year, so be sure to partake in the festival for a chance to earn them.

This patch contains reworks to Water Buckets and storage containers, as well as new kinds of storage container items.

Chest-type storage containers have new recipes and names, and storage amounts have been rebalanced. More storage items have also been implemented, some of which specifically store items like clothing, crops, or herbs. Items like wardrobes and dressers are now functional, and can now be used to store clothing items.

Players who have more items in existing chests than they can currently hold will find an overflow chest near the entrance to their Homestead containing all the relocated items, as well as some additional free chests to help you reorganize. Additionally, if you have an existing wardrobe, you will need to pick it up and place it again in order to be able to use it as storage.

Water Buckets now contain five uses, which will make them more convenient to use and require less refilling. As a result, filled buckets will no longer stack in the inventory (empty buckets will still stack).
We've also made optimizations to reduce the game file size and you should notice improved load times across the board!

The following items are now functional storage: Tall Metal Shelving, Kitchen Pipe Shelving, Live Edge Shelves, Woven Baskets, Cedar Wardrobes, Metal Herb Drying Racks, Wildflower Dresser
If you have an existing wardrobe, you will need to pick it up and place it again in order to be able to use it as storage.

Players with more items than their current chests will hold will be able to reclaim their items from an overflow chest by the entrance to their Homestead, and will receive additional chests as compensation.

It's about time for a quick Developer Update on what we've been up to lately!

Just last week, we greatly streamlined the account creation and sign-in process. There's no longer any need to enter your login email and password - just open the game and you will be able to log in automatically, or create a Spellfarers character much faster if you're a first time player.

Our team is currently in the process of animating and implementing cutscenes for the major story quests — some of which have already been added to the game. notes.title: Version 0.600: Camera Updates, Sound Effects, and Bug Fixes!

items.text: Just in time for spring cleaning, today's update has introduced a long-awaited camera system revamp, finally bringing us to Version 0.600 of Spellfarers! Expect much smoother camera behaviour and better looking dialogue scenes in this release. Walls, stairs, and other terrain will feel a lot better and smoother to navigate on and around.

We've also added a ton of new sound effects for actions, another ongoing process. The audio for walking on grass also has been touched up, and for those with apiaries at their homestead, the furious buzzing of thousands of bees will be a little more subdued.
New Camera System!
Dinner Parties are now functional - invite your coven over and share some good food!

So, what's next now that we're onto 0.600 and beyond? Currently, one of our focuses is working on cutscenes for many dialogue sequences, like the personal quests for the various townsfolk. One of Jinni's quests, Smelted Souvenir, has already had this incorporated in today's update, in fact! More are in the storyboarding and development stage right now and will be making their way into the game over time to give the local townsfolk a chance for their unique personalities and stories to shine.

Beyond that, we've got a big rework of Tile Mode in the future to make decorating your homestead and placing furniture a smoother experience, so you can feel encouraged to get creative with your space and the new items you acquire over time.
Remember to join the Discord to share your feedback and discuss the latest updates and upcoming changes!

Hello 2025 - and Year of the Snake!

It's the first Developer Update of the new year and we've been back at full development pace on Spellfarers for a little while, having recently welcomed an additional programmer to the Digital Leisure team! So, here's a quick look at where we are and what's in the works next.

One of the current major focuses of development continues to be the NPC animation updates. We've been implementing more animations for the townsfolk, updating pathing and routines, and overall making the residents of Wenngrove more lively and expressive. You'll continue to see more gradual improvements and updates as we smooth out the rough edges and add more animations.
Full controller support is another thing that will be ready soon, with the addition of an on-screen keyboard and more functionality. This also means better compatibility for Steam Deck players.
We've also been planning out a revamp of the camera system which will reduce clipping, improve dialogue scenes, and overall make the camera much smoother.
More starting character customization options are also in the works, and we're updating the default player avatar templates for new players to work from to make use of them.
We're approaching a milestone version number in the near future! Thanks for playing, Witches, and we'll be back with another Developer Update with Version 0.600!

The year is coming to a close, so it's time for one more Spellfarers Developer Update!
If you haven't checked in on Spellfarers development in a while, here's a quick update on some of the larger feature updates:
-Revamped progression and homestead upgrades
-Backpack and Tool Belt upgrades
-Fishing rework
-Much, much more

We've had some more major updates lately between updates to fishing, progression, and land expansion; including this week's Tool Belt addition and mining/treecutting changes. We're now comfortably approaching the end of Phase 1 on our development roadmap:

Minor economy updates are always possible in the future, but we're pretty happy with the overall state of the in-game economy at present. There are still some additional things in the works for the Phase 1 component of storage upgrades and expansions, but soon enough we'll be moving onto Phase 2: Fun and Functionality.

Phase 2 will make things feel a lot livelier in the town of Wenngrove, adding much more animation to the residents and their daily schedules, polish, a new character in Hannan, and more. We'll also focus more on iterating and polishing the menu and UI systems during this time to achieve full controller support in addition to mouse and keyboard.
The pace of updates will naturally slow down later into December as the holiday season approaches, but we're not done for the year just yet!
Thanks for continuing to follow along during our Early Access development! We look forward to making even bigger strides in the new year and working towards the Spellfarers 1.0 release in 2025.

It's every Witch's favourite season! We're now over two months into Early Access and we have a brief developer update on what we're doing and where we're headed. The update pace is a little less breakneck than the past days of early access lately, but lots of work is continuing behind the scenes and the team has been expanding!

Lately, we've been making adjustments to the early experience based on your feedback, with new early game quests and other features to help players become familiar with the Minor Transmutation Spell once they've unlocked it and learn what kind of materials it can be used to create. Most items now have their descriptions properly implemented, which will ease the learning curve - some spell descriptions still to come in the near future.

We've also introduced some UI improvements that should make it clear how much progress has been made on harvesting resource nodes. As of last week's update, progress bars now appear when mining or chopping trees to nearby players so you can see your progress and make it easier to join in and work together with fellow Witches.

In the very near future, we are continuing an ongoing overhaul of the menu systems, standardizing their layouts and improving visuals and polish. We'll also be refining the new features above, so we'd love to hear your impressions on them!

Looking ahead, we have plans to make upgrades more available and visible, so that players have additional direction via items, quests, and dialogue to help them actually learn about and reach new and existing upgrades. These upgrades will include expansion of things like storage, gardening plots, and homestead features - say goodbye to the struggle of trying to keep all your stuff organized with just one chest to work with!
That's all for now - but remember to join the official Discord where we'll be posting some exclusive sneak peeks of some things we've been working on.

It’s been a whirlwind here at the office the last few weeks. Early Access has been live for 14 business days, and we’ve released just as many patches. Whew!

While we’re swatting down bugs as fast as possible, we wanted to give you an update on what’s going on at the office with regards to some of our longer-term targets. (Given that we’re patching daily so far, “longer term” in this case means hopefully within the next few weeks.)

Quests and balancing are still top of mind for us.: We’ve finished a first pass at re-jigging some of the requirements to get a noticeboard quest. A lot of early-game noticeboard quests will have their turn-in requirements reduced and should be easier to complete. Many later-game quests have been pushed further out, so you shouldn’t get those quests until you have the ability to make or get the required items.: Following this, we are planning to adjust reward values to better reflect item costs, and make the quests available more often. This does mean that favor values will be adjusted down, but given the increased availability of quests, this should mean it won’t hurt as much to turn down a quest you don’t want to do, and overall make it easier to earn favor.

We’ve heard your storage woes, and will work on making more storage available more quickly.: Ah, the bane of every RPG – the inventory management game. While we do have options for expanding storage in a variety of ways, literally all of them are too harshly gated. We’ll be adjusting those down in the near future to make it easier to store your stuff. This is slated for review early next week, and will take some time to implement.

Controls and Accessibility passes to make it easier for everyone to play.: We really appreciate your feedback on this one. Camera controls, fishing, and being able to hold instead of tapping buttons for harvesting trees etc. are top of our list in this category. Adjustments to these items will be ongoing, as it affects a variety of interfaces, and will therefore take some time. But it is a priority for us that everyone can play in a way that is comfortable for them.: Thank you again, as always, to our players for your reports and feedback! With your help, we will keep building, bug swatting, and making things better!

notes.title: Developer Update - One Week of Early Access!

items.text: One of the common points of feedback we've read is with respect to shards and progression. We wanted to provide a quick developer update touching on these concerns and our plans going forward regarding this, as well as how later stages of the game will affect this. Some issues are being addressed now, others are in consideration for future improvements.

Some players are getting stuck on quests that are either too expensive, or buggy. This impacts progression, and players aren't getting the shards that we had expected. (Fireflies, straw bales, etc.): In the short term, we are fixing affected quests (such as the Ilo fix in this patch). Harder quests will be moved further down the progression line as needed.: In the long term, we will be making more daily quests that are easier to do. Where possible these should be instructive, showing you more about what the game has to do in the early game.

Some players are using their shards at the apothecary a lot more than anticipated, resulting in faster shard usage than expected.: Currently, transmuting the reagents you need should be the answer more often than not. If there is a case where purchasing from Zoji is a cheaper solution, let us know. We may need to communicate better that we view Zoji as a vendor to be used for a few purchases once in a while for most people to fill out some missing ingredients.

As the days go on, players will start to approach larger milestones with their favour such as apprenticeship. Here is how things will eventually play out once you eventually reach those longer-term milestones and how that will help with shard costs.: Once you reach enough favour with someone, you can choose to apprentice for them. You will only be able to apprentice for one trade at a time. That person will then ask you to do a larger, more time-consuming and costly quest; such as transmuting 15 Peonies. However, these quests will unlock additional rewards like the ability to purchase Peonies for Gold. This will be the case for most of your growable/fishable/forageable items.: Getting more easy early quests should ease the pains of shard costs and early progression. Gold will later be a much more useful resource, once you can use it to purchase the next tier of items.: We expect a lot of discussion around this and we appreciate all the feedback so far! We hope you all will feel like you are making more informed decisions with your shards, knowing more of how things will progress.

Wilds foraging. Stone is currently the go-to method for gold.: The merchants have received enough stone by now, so we're nerfing gold for stone. Sorry. But also, more plots! All players will begin with 24 maximum plots to play with going forward. Further down the line we want to give you more things to do to earn your gold (and favour) particularly in the early game - which we are all still in!

Spellfarers is a week into Early Access and it has been an extremely helpful week! Thank you for sharing your feedback and your experience with this game and we can't wait to continue building and improving Spellfarers!
